from fractions import Fraction as F
import math

# Claim: a simple (non-self-intersecting) curve of infinite length can lie in a bounded set.
# Witness: Koch curve. Level-n polygons are simple, length (4/3)^n -> infinity, all inside a fixed box.
# Points are stored in skew coordinates (a,b) = a + b*w, w = e^{i*pi/3}.
# Intersection tests are affine-invariant, so they stay exact in these coordinates.

def rot60(v):
    a, b = v
    return (-b, a + b)  # (a + b*w) * w, using w^2 = w - 1

def koch(pts):
    out = [pts[0]]
    for i in range(len(pts) - 1):
        P, Q = pts[i], pts[i + 1]
        d = ((Q[0] - P[0]) / 3, (Q[1] - P[1]) / 3)
        A = (P[0] + d[0], P[1] + d[1])
        r = rot60(d)
        Bp = (A[0] + r[0], A[1] + r[1])
        C = (P[0] + 2 * d[0], P[1] + 2 * d[1])
        out += [A, Bp, C, Q]
    return out

def cross(o, a, b):
    return (a[0] - o[0]) * (b[1] - o[1]) - (a[1] - o[1]) * (b[0] - o[0])

def onseg(p, q, r):
    return min(p[0], r[0]) <= q[0] <= max(p[0], r[0]) and min(p[1], r[1]) <= q[1] <= max(p[1], r[1])

def intersect(p1, p2, p3, p4):
    d1 = cross(p3, p4, p1); d2 = cross(p3, p4, p2)
    d3 = cross(p1, p2, p3); d4 = cross(p1, p2, p4)
    if ((d1 > 0 and d2 < 0) or (d1 < 0 and d2 > 0)) and ((d3 > 0 and d4 < 0) or (d3 < 0 and d4 > 0)):
        return True
    if d1 == 0 and onseg(p3, p1, p4): return True
    if d2 == 0 and onseg(p3, p2, p4): return True
    if d3 == 0 and onseg(p1, p3, p2): return True
    if d4 == 0 and onseg(p1, p4, p2): return True
    return False

def seglen2(P, Q):
    a, b = Q[0] - P[0], Q[1] - P[1]
    return a * a + a * b + b * b  # |a + b*w|^2 exactly
